facts.value: Active, passive, and assisted cues people observe and adopt about their own health.
Preventing or minimizing the effects of a disease, usually a chronic condition, through integrative care.
Practices to prevent infection and illness such as bathing and washing hands with soap, brushing and flossing teeth, and storing, preparing and handling food safely.
Information gleaned from personal observations of daily living may be used to inform personal decisions and actions.
The maintenance of strong social relationships, volunteering, and other social activities have been linked to positive mental health and increased longevity.
Frequent volunteering was associated with reduced risk of dying compared with older persons who did not volunteer.
Volunteering retirees had significantly better cognitive performance scores and better mental well-being than non-volunteering retirees.
Prolonged psychological stress may negatively impact health.
Application of methods to either reduce stress or increase tolerance to stress.
Physical methods used to relieve stress.
Methods include cognitive therapy, meditation, and positive thinking which work by reducing response to stress.
Improving relevant skills, such as problem solving and time management skills, reduces uncertainty and builds confidence, reducing reaction to stress-causing situations.
